short: The last emperor to rule as well as reign, for three years, before civil war split the court in two.
full:
Go-Daigo took the throne in 1318 as an adult of thirty, unusual in itself, and refused the role the Kamakura shogunate had defined for the court. Two plots against it were uncovered, in 1324 and 1331, and after the second he was exiled to the Oki Islands. He escaped in 1333. With Kusunoki Masashige holding out in the hills of Kawachi, Ashikaga Takauji turning on his masters at Kyoto and Nitta Yoshisada storming Kamakura itself, the shogunate fell within months.

The personal rule that followed lasted three years. It rewarded courtiers over the warriors who had won it, and in 1336 Takauji drove Go-Daigo from Kyoto and installed a rival emperor from the other branch of the family. Go-Daigo fled south to Yoshino with the imperial regalia, insisting his was the legitimate court, and died there in 1339 still claiming the throne. The schism he began outlasted him by half a century, and the question of which line had been legitimate was still being argued in Japanese schools in 1911.
